equation_request.abstract: We present several families of graphs that allow both efficient quantum walk implementations and efficient quantum walk based search algorithms. For these graphs, we construct quantum circuits that explicitly implement the full quantum walk search algorithm, without reference to a ‘black box’ oracle. These circuits provide a practically implementable method to explore quantum walk based search algorithms with the aim of eventual real-world applications. We also provide a numerical analysis of a quantum walk based search along a twisted toroid family of graphs, which requires O($\sqrt{n}$ log($n$)) elementary 2-qubit quantum gate operations to find a marked node.

specification.problem: Construct families of graphs admitting efficient quantum walk implementations and quantum-walk-based search, with explicit quantum circuits implementing the full search algorithm (no black-box oracle), and numerically analyze search on a twisted toroid graph family needing O(sqrt(n) log(n)) two-qubit gates to find a marked node.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level reconstruction: problem statement and the stated gate-complexity scaling only; graph definitions, coin/shift operators, circuit details and numerical data are not given in the abstract.

registers.name: position
registers.role: Encodes the graph node label for the walk

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Encodes the edge direction/coin state for the walk (assumed coined walk)

specification.initial_state: Assumed uniform superposition over all n nodes in the position register, with coin register in a uniform or fixed state.

steps.description: Prepare the initial state: uniform superposition over nodes (assumed).

Repeatedly apply a circuit-implemented search step: marking operation (flip coin on marked node, implemented without a black-box oracle) followed by the coin and shift walk operator on the graph, for a number of iterations on the order of sqrt(n) (assumed).
Decompose each walk step into elementary 1- and 2-qubit gates; total cost is stated as O(sqrt(n) log n) 2-qubit gates for the twisted toroid family.

specification.measurement: Assumed: after the roughly sqrt(n) search iterations, measure the position register in the computational basis to obtain a node label; the marked node is expected to be found with high probability (the abstract gives no explicit success probability).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Assumed: check whether the measured node is the marked one; if not, repeat the run. The abstract does not specify this procedure.
assumptions: Coined discrete-time walk structure, register layout, and sqrt(n) iteration count are assumed, not stated in the abstract.
Coined discrete-time walk with position and coin registers assumed.
Measurement of the position register and a repeat-until-success check are assumed, not stated in the abstract.
Measurement of the position register in the computational basis, with repeat-until-success verification, is assumed.
